desc:
You are given a string s of lowercase letters. You also have an empty stack t and an empty output string p. Two moves are allowed:

  • push: remove the first character of s and put it on top of t;
  • pop: remove the top character of t and append it to the end of p.

You keep moving until both s and t are empty. Return the lexicographically smallest string p that you can produce.

Examples: 'bac' gives 'abc' (push b, push a, pop a, pop b, push c, pop c). 'bdda' gives 'addb'.
constraints: s consists of lowercase English letters
hints: The first output letter must be some letter that is reachable, so think about what you want to pop and when.
Popping the top is never harmful when it is not larger than every letter still waiting in s. Why?
Precompute suffixMin[i], the smallest letter in s[i:]. After pushing s[i], pop while the top is ≤ suffixMin[i+1]. At the end pop everything.
editorial: Greedy: the smallest possible next output letter is the smaller of the stack top and whatever can still arrive. If the stack top is not larger than every letter still in s, nothing better can come later, and popping it now is optimal (equal letters are fine to pop first, because the output is the same and keeping them would only block letters below them). If a strictly smaller letter is still waiting in s, we must push more characters until it gets to the top.

Implement this with suffixMin. For each character, push it, then while the stack is non-empty and its top is ≤ suffixMin[i+1] (use a letter after 'z' for the empty suffix) pop it to the output. After the last character the stack is emptied from top to bottom. Each character is pushed and popped once: O(n) time, O(n) space.
